Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:11:1.hebrew: בצריך הכירא - קרא לבכור הוא דאתא, וכגון שבא ממדינת הים ולא הוחזק לנו בבכור אלא על פי אביו. ופרכינן: למאי הלכתא אשמעינן קרא דאביו נאמן עליו? ליטול פי שנים? פשיטא דנאמן, ל"ל קרא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:11:1.english: When he requires identification - The verse comes [to refer] to a firstborn, and [it is a case] such as where he arrived from overseas and was not established for us as a firstborn except by his father's word. And we ask: With regard to what halakha did the verse inform us that his father is believed concerning him? To receive a double portion? It is obvious that he is believed; why do I need a verse?

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:11:2.hebrew: מגו דאי בעי למיתב ליה - כולהו נכסי יהיב ליה, מהימן נמי למיתבינהו ניהליה בדיבורו בתורת בכורה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:11:2.english: Since if he wanted to give [it] to him - He could give him all the property, [so] he is also trusted to give them to him by his word under the law of the firstborn.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:12:1.hebrew: לאחר מיכן - לאחר שאמר לפנינו: ״בכור הוא״, נפלו לו. והוא רוצה לילך לדרך רחוקה, ומעיד עליו שאם יפלו נכסים של אב או אחד ממורישים לפניו בחייו — יטול זה בהן חלק בכורה. דלהכי, אי לאו דאשמעינן קרא, ליכא מיגו ד״אי בעי למיתבינהו״, דהשתא לא מצי יהיב, דאין אדם מקנה דשלב"ל, והשתא שקיל להו בתורת ירושה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:12:1.english: At a later point - [That is,] after he said before us, “He is the firstborn,” [the property] came into his possession. And he wishes to go on a distant journey, and testifies about him that if property of [his] father or one of [his other] bequeathers should come into his possession during his lifetime, this [son] shall take a firstborn’s portion in them. For regarding this, were it not that the verse informed us, there would be no miggo that “if he wanted to give them [he could have given them],” as right now he is unable to give [them], since a person cannot transfer ownership of an entity that has not come into the world; and now he takes them by virtue of inheritance.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:13:1.hebrew: כשהוא גוסס - לאחר שהעיד, כך אהני ליה: שאם יפלו לו נכסים כשהוא גוסס, שיטול זה בהן חלק בכורה. ואי לאו דהימניה קרא לאב להכירו — משום מגו לא זכה בהן, דמודה רבי מאיר באומר: "נכסים שיבואו לי כשאהיה גוסס נתונים לך", שלא אמר כלום, הואיל ובשעה שבאים לעולם לאו בר מתנה הוא. ולהכי נקט "כשהוא גוסס", ולא נקט "לאחר מיתה" — דהנהו, אפי' בתורת בכורה לא מהני ליה דבוריה, דאין הבכור נוטל בראוי כבמוחזק. והיינו ראוי: שכשמת עדיין לא היה מוחזק בהן, אבל ראויין לבא לו; ורחמנא אמר (דברים כא): "בכל אשר ימצא לו":
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:13:1.english: When he is moribund - After he testified [that this son is the firstborn], this is how it is effective for him: that if property should fall to [the father] when he is moribund, this [son] will take the portion of the firstborn in it. And were it not that the verse believed the father to acknowledge him, he would not have acquired [it] on account of a miggo, for Rabbi Meir concedes regarding one who says: "Property that will come to me when I am moribund is given to you," that he has said nothing, since at the time that they come into the world, he is not capable of [giving] a gift. And that is why [the Gemara] formulated: "When he is moribund," and did not formulate: "After death" — for [as for] those, even under the law of the firstborn, his statement would not be effective for him, as a firstborn does not take of prospective [property] as of possessed [property]; and this is [the definition of] prospective [property]: that when he died he was not yet in possession of them, but they were prospective to come to him; and the Merciful One stated (Deuteronomy 21:17): "In all that is found with him."

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:14:1.english: If his [betrothal] preceded, his betrothal is a [valid] betrothal - For he canceled the agency of the agent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:14:2.english: If his preceded, his betrothal is [a valid] betrothal - For he nullified the agency of the agent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:14:3.english: And if it is not known - It is not known which [of them] preceded.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:1:1.hebrew: האי קרא רישא בכ"ג - דכתיב: ״אלמנה וגרושה לא יקחו כי אם בתולות״, והא ליתיה אלא בכ"ג:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:1:1.english: This verse, the first clause addresses a case with a High Priest - For it is written: “A widow and a divorcee they shall not take, but rather virgins,” and this restriction applies only to a High Priest.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:1:2.hebrew: וסיפא בכהן הדיוט - דקאמר: ״בתולות מזרע בית ישראל והאלמנה אשר תהיה אלמנה מכהן יקחו״. וקס"ד דה"ק: שהיא אלמנה ממיוחס הראוי להשיא לכהונה, כדדריש ליה רבי יהודה לקמן: ״מן המשיאים לכהונה״. ואלמנה שתהא מותרת לכהן, לא משכחת לה אלא כהן הדיוט; והיכי מיפסק קרא ממילא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:1:2.english: And the latter clause [addresses] a common priest - For it states: “Virgins of the seed of the house of Israel; and a widow that is a widow of a priest, they may take” (Ezekiel 44:22). And it entered [our] mind that this is what it means: that she is a widow of [a man of] fit lineage who is eligible to marry [his daughter] into the priesthood, as Rabbi Yehuda expounds it below: “From those who marry [their daughters] into the priesthood.” And a widow who would be permitted to a priest, you find only [in the case of] a common priest; and how could the verse split on its own [between two subjects]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:1:3.hebrew: מן המשיאין לכהונה - אלמנת אדם שראוי להשיא בתו לכהונה יקחו, למעוטי אלמנת גר. ורבי יהודה לטעמיה, דאמר לעיל דאיירי יחזקאל אסמכתא בבת גר זכר, דכתיב: "מזרע בית ישראל" — כל זרע; בהאי קרא אורי לן אסמכתא דפוסל אשה בביאתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:1:3.english: From those who marry into the priesthood - They may take the widow of a man who is eligible to marry off his daughter into the priesthood, to exclude the widow of a convert. And Rabbi Yehuda [follows] his [own line of] reasoning, for he said above that Ezekiel was presenting an asmakhta regarding the daughter of a male convert, as it is written: “Of the seed of the house of Israel” — all the seed [must be from Israel; and] in this verse he indicated to us an asmakhta that [a convert] disqualifies a woman through his cohabitation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:2:1.hebrew: וכתב קרא הכי - בתמיה, דלא פריש ביה בהדיא דבגברא אחרינא בעי לאישתעויי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:2:1.english: And does Scripture write this way? - [This is asked] in astonishment: That it did not explicitly specify in it that it intends to speak about another person?

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:2:2.hebrew: ושמואל שוכב בהיכל ה' - חדא מילתא משמע, ועל כרחך מפסקינן ליה: ושמואל שוכב במקומו, בבית משמר הלויים שהיו שומרים את הבית. וכן תרגם יונתן: "בעזרת ליואי". והיכל — אנר קאי, שהמנורה היתה בהיכל משכן שילה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:2:2.english: “And Samuel was laid down to sleep in the Temple of the Lord” - [As written, this] implies a single matter, and perforce we must divide it: “And Samuel was laid down” [means] in his place, in the guardhouse of the Levites who were guarding the House. And so did [Targum] Yonatan translate: “In the courtyard of the Levites.” And [the phrase] “in the Temple” refers to the lamp, for the Menorah was in the sanctuary of the Tabernacle of Shiloh.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:3:1.hebrew: מכהן אין - אם היתה אלמנת כהן תינשא לכהן, אלמנת ישראל לא?! בתמיה. הרי לא הוזהר כהן הדיוט על אלמנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:3:1.english: From a priest, yes - If she was the widow of a priest, she may marry a priest, [but] the widow of an Israelite, [she may] not?! [This is asked] in astonishment: Behold, a common priest was not cautioned against [marrying] a widow.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:3:2.hebrew: משאר כהנים יקחו - לפרושי אתא דבכהן הדיוט קאי, והכי קאמר: והאלמנה אשר תהיה אלמנה — אפילו מישראל — משאר כהנים, שאינו כהן גדול, יקחו אותם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:3:2.english: Of the rest of the priests, they may take - It comes to explain that [the verse] is speaking of a common priest. And this is what it is saying: "And a widow who is a widow" — even [widowed] from an Israelite — "from the rest of the priests," [meaning] one who is not the High Priest, "they may take them."

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:4:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר נאמן - ארישא נמי פליג. בגמרא יליף טעמא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:4:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He is deemed credible - He disagrees with the first clause as well. In the Gemara, it derives the reason.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:4:2.hebrew: מן המשיאין לכהונה - אלמנת אדם שראוי להשיא בתו לכהונה יקחו, למעוטי אלמנת גר. ורבי יהודה לטעמיה, דאמר לעיל דאיירי יחזקאל אסמכתא בבת גר זכר, דכתיב ״מזרע בית ישראל״ — ״כל זרע״; בהאי קרא אורי לן אסמכתא דפוסל אשה בביאתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:4:2.english: From those who marry into the priesthood - [Priests] may take the widow of a person who is fit to marry off his daughter to the priesthood, to exclude the widow of a convert. And Rabbi Yehuda [follows] his reasoning, as he said above that Ezekiel was speaking as an asmakhta regarding the daughter of a male convert, as it is written: “Of the seed of the house of Israel” — [meaning] “the entire seed”; in this verse, he showed us an asmakhta that [a convert] disqualifies a woman through his intercourse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:4:3.hebrew: וכל שאי אתה נושא בתו - כגון גר, שפירשתי לך כבר — אי אתה נושא אלמנתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:4:3.english: And anyone whose daughter you may not marry - Such as a convert, as I have already explained to you — you may not marry his widow.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:6:1.hebrew: נשא - בת גר וגיורת, אין מוציאין מידו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:6:1.english: [If] he married - [The] daughter of a male convert and a female convert, we do not remove [her] from him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:7:1.english: He is a mamzer - That he was born to him from [a union with one of] those liable to karet.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:7:2.hebrew: אינו נאמן - דקרוב הוא אצלו, ואינו כשר להעיד עליו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:7:2.english: He is not believed - For he is related to him, and he is not fit to testify concerning him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:7:3.hebrew: ואפילו שניהם - האב והאם אומרים על עובר שבמעיה "ממזר הוא" — שאינו מן הבעל אלא מאיש אחר — אינן נאמנין. ובגמרא פריך: מאי אפי'? מאי רבותא דסיפא מדרישא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:7:3.english: And even both of them - The father and the mother say concerning a fetus in her womb, “It is a mamzer” — that it is not from the husband, but rather from another man — [yet] they are not believed. And in the Gemara it asks: What is [the meaning of] “even”? What novelty is there in the latter clause over the first clause?

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:7:4.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר נאמן - ארישא נמי פליג. בגמרא יליף טעמא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:7:4.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He is deemed credible - He also disagrees with the first clause. The Gemara derives the reason.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:8:1.hebrew: לא מבעיא איהו - האב, דלא קים ליה אם ממנו נתעברה או מאחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:8:1.english: It is not necessary [to state regarding] him - The father, as it is not clear to him whether she became pregnant from him or from another [man].

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:8:2.hebrew: לא מבעיא איהו - האב, דלא קים ליה אם ממנו נתעברה או מאחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:8:2.english: It is not necessary [to state regarding] him - The father, as it is not clear to him whether she became pregnant from him or from another.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:8:3.english: She is not believed - For [a person] is disqualified only through full testimony.

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:8:4.hebrew: ולא מיבעיא היכא דאית ליה חזקה דכשרות - כגון רישא, שכבר יצא לאויר העולם, ועד הנה הוחזק בחזקת כשר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:8:4.english: And it is not necessary [to state] where he has a presumption of unflawed lineage - Such as the first clause [of the Mishnah], where [the child] has already emerged into the airspace of the world, and until now was presumed to be of unflawed lineage:

Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:9:1.hebrew: אינו נאמן - אפסולא קיימי, אבל לענין בכור לא פליגי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 78b:9:1.english: He is not deemed credible - They are referring to the disqualification, but regarding the matter of a firstborn, they do not disagree.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 78b:13:1.hebrew: לא צריכא בנכסים דנפלו ליה כשהוא גוסס - ופי' בקונטרס: דאי לאו דהימניה קרא לאב להכירו משום מגו — דאי בעי מיתב ליה מי לא יהיב ליה — לא קא זכה בהו; דאפי' ר"מ, דאמר אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם, מודה באומר: "נכסים שיבואו לי כשאהיה גוסס נתונים לך", דלא אמר כלום, הואיל ובשעה שבאים לידו לאו בר מתנה הוא, דקסבר מתנה דגוסס לא מהניא, אבל היכא דבא מטעם בכורה מהניא. ולהכי נקט "כשהוא גוסס", ולא נקט "בנכסים שנפלו לאחר מיתה", דהא ודאי אפי' בתורת בכורה לא מהני ליה דיבוריה, דאין הבכור נוטל בראוי כבמוחזק, והיינו ראוי — דכשמת עדיין לא היה מוחזק בהן אבל ראויין לבא לו, ורחמנא אמר: "בכל אשר ימצא לו". משמע מתוך פירושו דנתינה דגוסס אינה כלום; וכמו כן יש מדקדקים דגוסס שרמז לכתוב גט לאשתו אין כותבין, דגוסס אין מעשיו כלום. וקשה, דבמסכת שמחות (פ"א) אמרינן: "הגוסס הרי הוא כחי לכל דבריו: נדרו נדר, והקדשו הקדש". ומיהו ההיא יש לדחות, דהתם היינו דוקא בנדר והקדש, דאמירתו לגבוה כמסירתו להדיוט, אבל בעלמא לא. ומ"מ קשה, דאמרי' בפ' מי שאחזו (גיטין דף ע:): "שחט בו שנים או רוב שנים, ורמז ואמר: כתבו ותנו גט לאשתי — יכתבו ויתנו"; ואין לך גוסס גדול מזה, שבודאי ימות! ובפרק כל הגט (גיטין דף כח.) נמי אמרינן: "המביא גט ממדינת הים והניחו זקן או חולה — נותנו בחזקת שהוא קיים". ודייק בגמרא: אמר רבא, לא שנו אלא שהניחו בחזקת שהוא חולה, אבל הניחו בחזקת שהוא גוסס — לא יתנו, דחיישינן שמא מת; משמע: הא אי ידעינן בודאי שעדיין הוא גוסס — נותנו בחזקת שהוא קיים, והוי גט; אלמא דגוסס כל דבריו קיימין! לכן נ"ל דודאי גוסס דבריו קיימין; והכא גבי מתנה, היינו טעמא דמתנתו אינה כלום — משום דמסתמא גוסס אינו יכול לדבר, אבל אם היה מדבר, פשיטא דדבריו קיימין. והא דנקט "גוסס" ולא נקט "חולה שנשתתק" — משום דמסתמא יתרפא ואז יהא בידו להקנות, אבל גוסס אין רגילות שיתרפא; וחולה נמי שנשתתק והרכין בראשו — דבריו קיימין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 78b:13:1.english: No, it is necessary [to explain the verse] with regard to property that fell to him when he was moribund [goses] - And Rashi explained that if the verse had not believed the father to recognize him [as the firstborn] based on a migo — for if he had wished to give [it] to him [as a gift], could he not have given [it] to him? — he would not have acquired them. For even Rabbi Meir, who says a person can transfer ownership of an entity that has not yet come into the world, concedes in [the case of] one who says, "Property that will come to me when I am moribund is given to you," that he has said nothing, since at the time it comes into his possession he is not capable of giving a gift, as he holds that the gift of a moribund person is not effective; but where it comes by virtue of the status of firstborn, it is effective. And for this reason [the Gemara] formulated [the case as] "when he was moribund," and did not formulate it as "property that fell after death," for with that, certainly, even under the law of firstborn status his statement would not be effective for him, as the firstborn does not take a double portion of [property that is merely] anticipated [ra'ui] as he does of [property that was] in possession [muḥzak]. And this is [the definition of] ra'ui: that when he died he was not yet in possession of them, but they were anticipated to come to him; and the Merciful One stated: "In all that is found with him" (Deuteronomy 21:17). It is implied from his explanation that the gift of a moribund person is nothing. And similarly, there are those who deduce that [in the case of] a moribund person who gestured [signaling] to write a bill of divorce [get] for his wife, they do not write [it], because [with] a moribund person, his actions are nothing. And this is difficult, for in Massekhet Semachot (chapter 1) we say: "A moribund person is like a living person in all matters: his vow is a vow, and his consecration is a consecration." However, that [ruling] can be dismissed, as there it is specifically regarding a vow and consecration, where one's statement to the Most High is equivalent to one's delivery to an ordinary person, but in general [transactions], no [it is not effective]. Nevertheless, it is difficult, for we say in the chapter [entitled] "Mi She'achazo" (Gittin 70b): If one slaughtered both [the trachea and the esophagus] in him, or the majority of both, and he gestured and said, "Write and give a get to my wife," they shall write and give [it]; and you have no greater moribund person than this, as he will certainly die! And in the chapter [entitled] "Kol HaGet" (Gittin 28a), we also say: If one brings a get from overseas and left him [the husband] elderly or sick, he gives it [to the wife] under the presumption that he is [still] alive. And the Gemara deduces: Rava said: They taught [this] only where he left him under the presumption that he was sick; but if he left him under the presumption that he was moribund, they may not give [it], for we are concerned that perhaps he died. This implies that if we knew with certainty that he was still moribund, he gives it under the presumption that he is alive and it is a valid get. Consequently, [with] a moribund person, all his words are legally valid! Therefore, it appears to me that certainly [with] a moribund person, his words are legally valid; and here, regarding a gift, this is the reason that his gift is nothing: because ordinarily a moribund person cannot speak, but if he were speaking, it is obvious that his words are legally valid. And as for [the Gemara] stating "moribund" and not stating "a sick person who became mute," [that is] because typically he will recover and then it will be in his power to transfer ownership, whereas with a moribund person, it is not common that he will recover; and also, a sick person who became mute and nodded with his head, his words are legally valid.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 78b:1:1.hebrew: האי קרא רישא בכ"ג - פירוש: דכתיב "אלמנה לא יקחו", וסיפא בכהן הדיוט — דכתיב "מזרע ישראל", ודרשינן: שנזרעו בתוליה, ומיירי בכל כהנים. וקשה: דמ"מ, "מזרע ישראל" קאי נמי לכ"ג כמו לכהן הדיוט! ונראה לפרש: רישא בכ"ג — דכתיב "אלמנה וגרושה לא יקחו כי אם בתולות", והא ליתא אלא בכ"ג; סיפא דקרא — דכתיב "והאלמנה אשר תהיה אלמנה מכהן יקחו", והיינו כהן הדיוט דוקא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 78b:1:1.english: "Concerning this verse, the first clause [deals] with a High Priest" - [One might suggest as an] explanation: For it is written, "A widow [and a divorcée] they shall not take," and the latter clause [deals] with a common priest, as it is written, "of the seed of [the house of] Israel," and we expound: whose virginity was formed [as an Israelite], which refers to all priests. Yet this is difficult: for in any case, "of the seed of Israel" applies also to a High Priest just as to a common priest! Rather, it appears [correct] to explain: "The first clause [deals] with a High Priest" — as it is written, "Neither a widow nor a divorced woman shall they take [to them for wives], but virgins," and this applies only to a High Priest; [and] the latter clause of the verse — as it is written, "and the widow that is the widow of a priest, they may take," and this is specifically a common priest.
